reply:
All four outputs are written, but the MJCF model is about 25% too light. Nine lofted printed bodies export as meshes with small gaps, so MuJoCo gives them no mass and no collision. Treat the simulation numbers below as approximate until that's fixed.

**1. MJCF** (`rex-mjcf/rex.xml`, standing pose, free base)
- **Bodies:** 164, with 163 meshes.
- **Joints and actuators:** 17 revolute joints, each driven by a position actuator. A keyframe is included.
- **Torque limits:** ±1.912 N·m for the 16 STS3215 servos and ±0.177 N·m for the SG90 jaw servo. The control ranges are the joint limits.
- **Total mass:** 1.263 kg. The CAD model weighs 1.676 kg, so about 413 g is missing.
- **Open-mesh bodies:** TorsoShell, Thigh_L/R, Foot_L/R, Skull, Jaw and Claws_L/R. The CAD solids are closed; the gaps appear when they're turned into meshes. I re-imported the Foot_L mesh to check: its volume matches the CAD to 0.02%, but it has a few open edges. The exporter has no mesh-quality setting, so I couldn't fix this here. The feet still touch the ground through the closed sole pads.
- The exporter also warned that `ArmourPlate` "is not grounded: fixed where it is".

**2. Render** (`rex-render.png`, 1600 × 1000)
- **Camera:** low three-quarter front view from +X/−Y, about 10 cm above the ground. TinyRex fills about 93% of the frame height.
- **Pose:** jaw open 30°, head turned 20° toward the camera. I also tilted the head down to −45°: at the standing value of +10° the snout points straight up and doesn't look fierce. A check of the head and neck parts in this pose found no clashes, only existing contacts under 0.1 mm.
- **Workaround:** the first render check refused the scene: about 293k triangles against a limit of 262,144. For the render only, I hid 46 parts the camera can't see: the electronics inside the torso and their screws, the screws on top of the armour plate and inside the torso, and the screws on the back faces of the brackets. That brought it to 254,489. Everything is visible again in the saved file.

**3. BOM** (`rex-bom.csv`): 71 rows covering 163 parts, so 72 lines with the header. I worked that out from the export's reply because I had no way to open the file.
- The rows include 16 STS3215 and 1 SG90 servos, and 84 socket-head screws: 24 M2x6, 32 M2x8, 8 M2x10, 2 M2.5x8, 4 M2.5x10, 6 M3x6 and 8 M3x10.
- The printed parts and envelopes have empty part-number and description columns; their names are in the definition column.
- Each servo horn is its own row instead of sitting under its servo.

**4. Stand simulation** (MuJoCo 3.16, 2 s): it holds.
- **Result:** it didn't fall, maximum tilt was 0.08° and the base dropped 0.3 mm.
- **Utilisation (peak torque):** no servo saturated.

| Servo | Left | Right |
|---|---|---|
| Knee | 5.2% | 6.0% |
| Hip roll | 2.3% | 1.3% |
| Ankle pitch | 0.8% | 1.1% |
| Ankle roll | 0.6% | 0.7% |
| Hip pitch | 0.0% | 0.3% |
| Hip yaw | 0% | 0% |

  Head pitch 1.3%, neck pitch 0.2%, jaw 0.2%, head yaw 0.0%, tail yaw 0%.
- These figures come from the light model. Scaling them up for the missing mass still leaves every servo under 10%.

**Final checks**
- After the render I put the standing pose back (hip pitch −20°, knee −40°, ankle pitch −20°, neck −40°, head pitch +10°, everything else 0) and confirmed every joint value matches the original.
- All 163 bodies still have their colours: lime printed shells, #111111 for the armour plate, spikes, claws, eye sockets, brow ridges and sole pads, #EDEDED teeth, and the servos, electronics and screws in their library colours.
- Nothing is grounded and no parts are left unattached.
- Saved to `s7_export.polykrom`. That file also keeps the render camera as a setup named "hero". This stage built no new parts, so I saved once, at the end.
